placements.why: This envelope's entire content is an observatory instrument's calibration record: a stated calibration value, tied to verification against a named reference standard (the June plates), for a named instrument (Kestrelwood spectrograph). Nothing in the (empty) existing strata covers organizational calibration/proof-of-instrument-state, and 'Calibration' is exactly the kind of foundational, parent-less organizational category this content names — it needs no Architecture/Proof ancestor minted first, matching the rule that a strata mint is usually the normal no-parent case.
placements.title: Instrument calibration state becomes its own organizational record, traceable to a verification standard
placements.frame: What is being established here about an instrument's readiness — that it is calibrated, and that the calibration has been checked against a fixed reference standard?

placements.title: Calibration soundness is established by verification against a fixed reference standard, not by the calibration figure alone
placements.frame: Does this calibration claim rest on demonstrated verification against a named, fixed reference standard — and does that verification hold across the relevant operating range — or is the figure asserted without that anchor?
placements.why: src-1 states the calibration and explicitly grounds it in verification against the June reference plates, holding across the full observing band; src-2 and src-3 restate the same instrument and calibration fact in labeled-field form (fc-1 footing), with src-3 repeating the verification-against-reference-plates language. Per the position-pass read, all three converge on one theme, stated three ways: calibration validity is established through reference-standard verification. This passes the narrative grain test — it names a recurring subject (how calibration soundness gets established) that future calibration envelopes for other instruments or other reference sets will keep feeding, not a one-off measurement; the specific 88.4 MHz figure and the June plates are the evidentiary facts supporting this theme, not leaves in themselves. Placed under the newly minted Calibration stratum as its first thematic leaf.
